A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FORS-based sampling research. The complete main texts, equations, algorithms, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching v1 Appendix F to v2 Appendix G.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, theoretical guarantees, and proofs, including in its appendices. Section 6 explicitly leaves implementation and experimental evaluation to future work.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout its main text and appendices. Section 6 still leaves implementation and experimental evaluation to future work.

M1.justification: Section 4 replaces v1's separate diffusion-sampling variants with a common proposal using the next-time score and adjusted Gaussian covariance. The corrector uses denoiser differences, a random Gaussian anchor, and revised path coefficients (v2 Equations 12–15). An optional final DDPM step is also introduced for sampling the original smooth distribution. The underlying FORS acceptance mechanism remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or test scenarios for empirical training or evaluation. Added distributional examples and applicability conditions are theoretical.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. Revised comparisons with other sampling algorithms concern theoretical guarantees and research positioning.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an experimental evaluation protocol. Changes to analytical step-size conditions and divergence guarantees belong to the method and theory assessments.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness experiments, or empirical case studies. The revised score-error and Gaussian-approximation analyses are mathematical derivations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Probability bounds in the theorems are not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither version contains empirical numerical results or qualitative experimental findings. Revised convergence and complexity bounds are assessed under T1 and C1.

T1.justification: v2 replaces the fixed-resolution intrinsic-dimension definition with one optimized over covering radius and capped by ambient dimension. Theorems 4.3 and 4.9 revise diffusion guarantees and score-error dependence, introducing Frobenius-norm and coverage assumptions. Appendices E–F substantially revise the supporting proofs and add Gaussian-kernel coverage bounds and a one-step KL characterization. The log-concave theorem largely survives as Theorem G.1.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.1 now claim intrinsic-dimension complexity under standard L2 score errors with constant amplification. v1 separated its ambient-dimension guarantee from a low-dimensional extension requiring stronger error control and a dimensional penalty. v2 also claims complexity governed by a Frobenius-norm parameter under explicit additional assumptions; this is not a direct comparison using v1's Lipschitz parameter.

C2.justification: v1 identifies worsened score-error dependence as a limitation and questions whether it is fundamental. v2's revised guarantees remove that qualification and explain applicability to manifolds, finite supports, and bounded-radius distributions. Appendix E.5 adds a substantive interpretation of Frobenius regularity as governing Gaussian approximation difficulty and motivates the proposal choice. Section 5 also explains the general log-concave guarantee through progress on KLS.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies implementation configurations, hardware information, released code, or data-access instructions. Both defer implementation, and the proximal-oracle implementation discussion is retained in the relocated log-concave appendix.

R1.justification: v2 adds quantized-score sampling and exact diffusion-simulation precedents, alongside references supporting new arguments. Section 1.2 and Appendix A.1 change the Gatmiry comparison from incomparable bounds to recovering the radius/noise dependence, up to logarithmic factors, under weaker score-error assumptions. These are focused positioning updates; several other reference changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: Section 4's three-method narrative is substantially reorganized around intrinsic dimension, a common algorithm, and refined assumptions. The appendices separate structural diffusion properties from sampler proofs, reorganize technical lemmas, and move retained log-concave material from F to G. Section 3.2 also expands the explanation of proposal construction.

P2.justification: Neither version contains conventional figures or result tables. Algorithm displays, particularly Algorithms 1 and 3, move relative to surrounding text, and mathematical blocks are repaginated. The single-column layout and pseudocode styling remain substantially the same.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain addresses v1's explicit score-error weakness: its low-dimensional theorem required error control under additional Gaussian convolutions and multiplied accumulated squared error by d/d_star. v2 provides a revised sampler and substantial supporting analysis for intrinsic-dimension sampling under ordinary L2 errors without that penalty (Theorem 4.3). This materially broadens the central guarantee's applicability. The sharper smoothness result has distinct Frobenius and coverage assumptions, which v2 states and analyzes explicitly rather than establishing an unconditional same-assumption speedup.
